title: Descriptive set 𝓕 is covertly normativised via content-bearing success S (faithfulness to quid facti)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
𝓕 (Def. 4) is defined via a content-bearing success criterion S, and Lemma 1 derives non-coincidence from S having 'endorsement-independent content.' But S (predictive accuracy, reliability) is itself a normative/epistemic notion whose endorsement-independence is exactly what is contested. Importing S into the *descriptive* set normativises the descriptive side and makes the 𝓕/𝓙 separation easier than the problem's clean quid-facti/quid-juris split allows. The problem wants quid facti? to be purely factual ('as a matter of fact ... with apparent success').

Fix: split 'apparent success' (purely behavioural, for 𝓕) from 'genuine reliability' (normative, for 𝓙); keep 𝓕 behavioural and redo Lemma 1's non-coincidence argument under the behavioural reading.
